subject: Chemistry
central_question: How do valence electrons and orbital interactions determine bond type, geometry, polarity, stability, and magnetism?
in_scope_units: Lewis approach, octet rule, formal charge, and resonance.
Bond parameters, polarity, and dipole moment.
Valence bond theory, overlap, sigma and pi bonds, and hybridisation.
Molecular orbital theory, bond order, and magnetism.

known_pitfalls.claim: The octet rule explains all molecules.
known_pitfalls.correction: It has incomplete, odd-electron, and expanded-octet exceptions.

known_pitfalls.claim: A double bond is exactly twice as strong.
known_pitfalls.correction: It contains one sigma and one pi bond, with different strengths.

known_pitfalls.claim: Hybrid and molecular orbitals are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Hybrid orbitals belong to one atom; MOs extend over a molecule.
MO theory predicts two unpaired electrons and paramagnetism.

recommended_example_progression: Use MO theory and hydrogen bonding.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use exercises on Lewis structures, formal charge, ionic bonding, geometry, hybridisation, bond parameters, molecular orbitals, magnetism, and hydrogen bonding.
